title: Upon the Gospel's Sacred Page
description: Upon the Gospel's Sacred Page in Tonic Solfa to MELCOMBE, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: John Bowring wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 296 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Progress of Gospel Truth”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to MELCOMBE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Up-on the Go-spel's sa-cred page The ga-thered beams of a-ges shine; And, as it ha-stens, ev-ery age But makes its bright-ness more di-vine.

lines: The gathered beams of ages shine;
And, as it hastens, every age
But makes its brightness more divine.
Truth, strengthened by the strength of thought,
Whence sagest teachers may be taught,
And Wisdom's self become more wise.
More glorious still as centuries roll,
New regions blest, new powers unfurled,
Its waters shall o'erflow the world;
Flow to restore, but not destroy;
As when the cloudless lamp of day
Pours out its floods of light and joy,
And sweeps each lingering mist away.

licence: Public domain: John Bowring died in 1872.
credits: Words by John Bowring (1792–1872), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to MELCOMBE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
